blocks.content:
q-Hodge complexes over the Habiro ring
Ferdinand Wagner
October 9, 2025
Abstract. — Peter Scholze has raised the question whether some variant of the
q-de Rham complex is already defined over the Habiro ring H := limm∈N Z[q]∧
(qm−1).
Such a variant should then be called (algebraic) Habiro cohomology.
We show that algebraic Habiro cohomology exists whenever the q-de Rham
complex can be equipped with a q-Hodge filtration: a q-deformation of the Hodge
filtration, subject to some reasonable conditions. To any such q-Hodge filtration we
associate a small modification of the q-de Rham complex, which

blocks.content:
[]{#sec:Intro label="sec:Intro"}

Throughout the introduction, we'll work over $\IZ$ for simplicity. In the main body, we'll work instead relative to a $\Lambda$-ring $A$ which is *perfectly covered* in the sense of [\[par:Notations\]](#par:Notations){reference-type="ref" reference="par:Notations"} below.

blocks.title: Habiro cohomology
blocks.content:
In this paper we'll investigate the following question, which was raised by Peter Scholze:

::: numpar
[]{#qst:Habiro label="qst:Habiro"} *Is there a version of $q$-de Rham cohomology with coefficients not in the power series ring $\IZ\qpower$, but in the Habiro ring $$\Hh\coloneqq \limit_{m\in\IN}\IZ[q]_{(q^m-1)}^\complete\,?$$*
:::

A cohomology theory that provides a positive answer to Question [\[qst:Habiro\]](#qst:Habiro){reference-type="ref" reference="qst:Habiro"} would then deserve the name *Habiro cohomology*. Let us first convince the reader that it should be worthwhile to search for

Having justified that Question [\[qst:Habiro\]](#qst:Habiro){reference-type="ref" reference="qst:Habiro"} is relevant, let us now summarise the contributions of this paper. As it turns out, Question [\[qst:Habiro\]](#qst:Habiro){reference-type="ref" reference="qst:Habiro"} is closely related to the following much less esoteric question:

::: numpar
[]{#qst:qHodgeFiltration label="qst:qHodgeFiltration"} *Is it possible to equip the $q$-de Rham complex with a $q$-deformation of the Hodge filtration?*
:::
